facts.text: The class is the Thorlabs K10CR1 rotation stage driver
The constructor takes the serial number, searches the serial ports for that device, and zeroes the backlash when the connection succeeded
connect() scans every serial port and matches the device by the serial number inside the port description, then opens the port at 115200 baud with a 0.1 s timeout
The FTDI chip of the controller has VID:PID 0403:faf0 according to the comment of connect()
The class converts an angle to its encoder unit as angle * 24576000 / 180 and back as counts * 180 / 24576000
The protocol commands are fixed byte frames written as hex text; the homing frame is '430401005001' and the jog frame is '6a0401015001'
home() writes the homing frame and reads 6 bytes of response
moverel() and moveabs() assemble the frame from the header, the channel word '0100' and the 4-byte encoder position; they do not read a response
jog() writes the jog frame and reads 20 bytes of response
getpos() writes the position query frame, reads 12 bytes, takes the last 4 as the position and returns degrees rounded to three decimals
identify() only writes the information frame and returns the byte count of the serial write, not an identity
zerobacklash() writes the backlash parameter with the position of 0 degrees
The clone README describes the repository as a Thorlabs K10CR1 rotation stage python driver
The clone's own test opens the stage by serial number and makes a relative move of -10 degrees
